items.title: Why Deploying Physical AI at Scale Demands Safety at Every Layer
items.summary: Deploying physical AI at scale necessitates safety considerations across the entire system, encompassing hardware, software, AI behavior, and the operating environment. Safety in physical AI requires a new model because dynamic environments demand context-aware adaptation, AI behavior needs assurance through testing, and ongoing deployment requires continuous validation. NVIDIA's Halos system provides a full-stack safety foundation for physical AI in autonomous vehicles and robotics, covering hardware, software, model, and simulation. This ecosystem allows for independent assessment and certification, ensuring that scaled physical AI systems are not just capable but also trustworthy. Ultimately, building functional safety from the start is crucial for creating scalable and deployable solutions.
items.audio_script: From NVIDIA Blog, "Why Deploying Physical AI at Scale Demands Safety at Every Layer". This report details the necessity of comprehensive safety considerations across all layers of physical AI deployment, emphasizing that safety requires a new model to address dynamic environments and continuous validation. The development of the Halos system provides a full-stack safety foundation for physical AI in areas like autonomous vehicles and robotics by covering hardware, software, model, and simulation. This ecosystem enables independent assessment and certification, ensuring that scaled physical AI systems possess both capability and trustworthiness through rigorous testing and simulation processes. Building functional safety into the initial design phase is identified as crucial for creating scalable and deployable solutions in the AI technology sector.

items.title: ROS Discourse General: From CT Scan to Robotic Surgery Prototype: Kidney Stone Detection & PCNL Planning in ROS 2
items.summary: A research prototype connects medical CT scans to ROS 2 visualization and robot simulation for kidney stone detection and PCNL planning. The pipeline involves segmenting organs, detecting stones via high-HU thresholds, and creating 3D meshes. A planner ranks access corridors based on anatomical constraints to determine optimal needle paths. The system visualizes these paths in RViz and simulates the robot's movement using a Franka FR3. This system serves as a learning MVP for geometric planning and kinematic replay, not a clinical tool.
items.audio_script: From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: From CT Scan to Robotic Surgery Prototype: Kidney Stone Detection & PCNL Planning in ROS 2". This report details a research prototype linking medical CT scans to ROS 2 visualization and robot simulation for kidney stone detection and percutaneous nephrolithotomy planning. The methodology involved segmenting organs from the scan data, detecting stones using high-Hounsfield unit thresholds to generate three-dimensional meshes, and subsequently using a planner to rank access corridors based on anatomical constraints to determine optimal needle paths. These paths were then visualized within RViz and simulated using a Franka FR3 robot, establishing a learning minimum viable product for geometric planning and kinematic replay. This development indicates progress in applying robotics and artificial intelligence to complex surgical planning workflows. Future research will focus on advancing this system toward clinical application.

items.title: Accelerating a ROS 2 Node with an AI Agent and NVIDIA Isaac ROS
items.summary: ROS 2 can exchange GPU-resident payloads via zero-copy transport using the `rosidl::Buffer` and a CUDA buffer backend. NVIDIA Isaac ROS 5.0 updates all nodes to utilize this backend for more efficient data movement. An AI coding agent, using the `migrate-node-to-rosidl-buffer` skill, audits and refactors existing CUDA-accelerated nodes to adopt this feature. This process preserves ROS 2 message interfaces while optimizing data transfer between nodes. The methodology allows for a repeatable, agent-driven workflow to accelerate GPU-heavy robotics applications on platforms like the Jetson AGX Thor.
items.audio_script: From NVIDIA Developer Blog, "Accelerating a ROS 2 Node with an AI Agent and NVIDIA Isaac ROS". This report details a method for accelerating ROS 2 node performance by enabling GPU-resident payload exchange through zero-copy transport. The methodology involves utilizing the rosidl::Buffer and a CUDA buffer backend for data movement within the ROS 2 framework. NVIDIA Isaac ROS 5.0 updates mandate the use of this backend for improved data efficiency across all nodes. An AI coding agent, employing the migrate-node-to-rosidl-buffer skill, was used to audit and refactor existing CUDA-accelerated nodes to adopt this feature. This process maintains ROS 2 message interfaces while optimizing inter-node data transfer, establishing a repeatable, agent-driven workflow for GPU-heavy robotics applications. This advancement suggests a pathway for significantly faster development cycles in GPU-accelerated robotics systems.

items.title: ROS Discourse General: Oh noes! What's going on with Anubis?
items.summary: The author is intermittently encountering an error message when attempting to access ROS documentation, such as the C++ API. The author is seeking confirmation if others are experiencing this issue. The author has checked their settings, noting that browser cookies are enabled and they are not using a VPN. The error messages were obtained by browsing to a specific location. The post is asking if this is a widespread problem.
items.audio_script: From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: Oh noes! What's going on with Anubis?". This report details intermittent errors encountered by a user when attempting to access ROS documentation, specifically the C++ API. The user sought confirmation regarding whether this issue is widespread across the community. The author confirmed that settings, including browser cookies, were enabled, and no virtual private network was in use when the error messages were observed after navigating to a specific documentation location. The inquiry focused on determining if this was a widespread problem affecting other users. The situation suggests a potential issue with access or documentation rendering within the ROS framework. Further investigation into system-wide access protocols is warranted by the community.

items.title: CHOREO: Every Humanoid Skill as a Trajectory
items.summary: Recent advances in humanoid robotics have produced diverse skills, but they remain siloed due to incompatible representations. CHOREO is a framework for training-free composition of heterogeneous humanoid skills by viewing every skill as an executable motion trajectory. It introduces SkillMotion, a unified representation combining motion states, contacts, semantics, and boundary conditions for each capability. Skills can be composed using direct continuation, blending, or bridge motions without retraining source models. Experiments on Unitree G1 showed that organizing SkillMotion assets achieved high success rates across multi-action tasks.

items.title: D3DWA: Adaptive Weight and Prediction-Horizon for Dynamic Window Approach via Dueling Double Deep Q-Network
items.summary: The D3DWA framework is enhanced by D3DWA, which adapts the Dynamic Window Approach using a Dueling Double Deep Q-Network. This adaptation allows the system to jointly select evaluation weights and a prediction horizon based on the current navigation state. Longer prediction horizons are suitable for open areas, while shorter ones are better for cluttered regions. Experiments in simulated environments and real-robot tests demonstrated that D3DWA successfully navigated various layouts. The results confirm the benefit of adaptively managing evaluation weights and prediction horizons.

items.title: DeViGrasp: Robust Visual Mobile Grasping for Quadruped Manipulators under Degraded Perception
items.summary: Quadruped manipulators struggle with whole-body control when visual perception is degraded by factors like occlusion and noise. DeViGrasp introduces DeViGrasp-Bench, a benchmark to systematically evaluate grasping under these visual degradations. The method proposes DeViGrasp-Net, a teacher-student framework combining grasp reasoning with reliability-aware temporal target estimation. This framework leverages dual-view segmented-depth data and memory mechanisms to improve performance under difficult conditions. DeViGrasp-Net significantly outperforms existing methods like VBC and DQ-Net across various degradation levels.

items.title: ORDER: A Fictitious-World Benchmark for Domain-Adaptive Embodied AI
items.summary: ORDER introduces a benchmark based on a fictitious world to evaluate Domain-Adaptive Embodied AI. It uses a synthetic corpus defining self-consistent physics that is absent from pre-training data. The benchmark includes a knowledge test and a compositional task for safe manipulation across familiar and novel scenes. Models that continually pre-train show genuine world-model induction, unlike memorization. Performance on the spatial task, not just knowledge testing, predicts real plan quality in embodied systems.

items.title: OJOx: Specification-Conditioned Demonstrations for Embodied AI in Construction
items.summary: Large-scale human demonstrations often lack the external specifications that define an action's purpose. OJOx introduces specification-conditioned demonstrations for embodied AI in construction by synchronizing perceived physical states, external design specifications, and the demonstrator's behavior. This system uses a capture interface to deliver design geometry to a headset and record it synchronously with whole-body and hand motions. The work presents a method for training embodied policies to act toward specifications not present in their training experience. Recorded sessions remain compatible with existing humanoid retargeting infrastructure for simulation and testing.

items.title: When Does Test-Time Physical Diagnosis Pay? A Frozen Policy Buys Evidence It Never Reads
items.summary: To effectively use test-time physical diagnosis for robot behavior, six ordered empirical conditions must be met. These conditions involve a meaningful reference, identifiability, evidence use, decision value, selection value, and safe realization. While these conditions hold in controlled environments, the process breaks down when transferred to unseen mechanisms concerning evidence use. A linear model based on trace increments can recover correct choices, indicating the trace is informative but unused. Therefore, successful physical identification does not guarantee useful adaptation; evaluation must pinpoint where the diagnostic chain fails.

items.title: EditWM: Event-Decomposed World Modeling with Incremental Correction for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
items.summary: EditWM proposes a world model for autonomous driving by decomposing future predictions into normal evolution and event-induced incremental corrections. It uses a trajectory-conditioned normal predictor, which is then refined by a correction decoder that generates bounded feature updates based on observation history. This correction is regulated by a learned gate, and the corrected features inform trajectory scoring via cross-attention. Evaluation on navtest scenes showed a 5.35% reduction in future-feature MSE and improved trajectory selection. The system achieved a high EPDMS score, demonstrating improved prediction and planning.

items.title: Embedding Physics Priors in Robot Learning: A Survey
items.summary: Physics-embedded robot learning integrates physical laws and constraints into learning algorithms to address robotics limitations. Physics priors offer robotics-specific inductive biases that can improve generalization, interpretability, and sample efficiency beyond purely data-driven methods. The survey reviews various approaches, including physics-guided inputs, model architectures, and loss functions, across different machine learning models. It covers applications such as dynamics learning, planning, prediction, control, and estimation, along with the associated software ecosystem. The work concludes that physics priors complement data-driven learning, fostering more generalizable and trustworthy robotic systems.

items.title: AffordanceWAM: Affordance-Aware Joint World-Action Modeling for Robot Manipulation
items.summary: AffordanceWAM is a generative World Action Model designed for robot manipulation by representing object-centric spatiotemporal affordances. It uses Scalar Affordance and Affordance Heatmaps to ground visual prediction in task-relevant objects and interaction regions. The model is built upon a pretrained video diffusion Transformer and employs separate World and Action Experts connected by Masked Joint Self-Attention. It jointly predicts future RGB observations, affordance fields, heatmaps, and continuous robot actions using a unified flow-matching objective. Experiments show AffordanceWAM provides performance gains over baselines in robot manipulation tasks.
